## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design a practical CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) governance program in a real multi-region data platform with complex lineage and traceability requirements. It evaluates understanding of data governance, incident management, and safe deployment patterns.

- **Minimal REST API**: Simple endpoints enable teams to create, update, and query CAPAs while maintaining audit trails through evidence attachments and lineage tracking.
- **Region Metrics**: Measuring MTTC, recurrence rates, and evidence completeness provides visibility into regional performance and helps identify systemic issues.
- **RCA Template**: A structured root cause analysis process ensures lessons learned are documented and translated into preventive actions.
- **Canary Rollout**: Gradual deployment with automated rollback minimizes risk when introducing changes to transformation jobs.

questions.explanation:
## Correct Answer
Use template.metadata.name: my-app-{{cluster}} so each generated Application gets a unique name based on the cluster value.

## Why Other Options Are Wrong
- Option B would create name collisions across clusters, since the same fixed name would be used for all generated Apps.
- Option C misuses the destination field; cluster differentiation for the Application name should come from the template name, not the destination.
- Option D defeats the purpose of a single ApplicationSet generating many apps and adds unnecessary maintenance.

## Key Concepts
- ApplicationSet templating
- Generators (cluster) and template.name placeholders
- Unique naming for generated Applications

## Real-World Application
- When deploying to many clusters, using cluster-derived names helps administrators quickly identify which App belongs to which cluster and simplifies drift and health monitoring.
